text:
devon: Heads up — at ~08:12 UTC we saw a burst of GPU pod evictions in us-west-2-gpu pool. ~120 pods restarted in ~3m. Kubelet events show transient network probe failures and then eviction.

ana: do you have the event lines? are these NodeLost or NetworkUnavailable?

devon: pasted the most relevant lines from node journal: 
```
Aug 12 08:11:56 node-uw2-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: W0812 08:11:56.782 health_prober.go:211] net-probe: probe RTT jitter 240ms, packet loss 27% -> marked Unhealthy
Aug 12 08:12:01 node-uw2-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: I0812 08:12:01.009 node_status.go:145] Setting NodeCondition NetworkUnavailable=True reason=NetProbeFailure
Aug 12 08:12:05 node-uw2-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: I0812 08:12:05.120 eviction_manager.go:367] Evicting pods to reclaim resources: reason=NetworkUnavailable
```

mike: that probe RTT/jitter number looks high, but it's usually transient after our network config rollouts. Were there maintenance jobs in the AZ at that time?

devon: yes, net team ran a firmware push to top-of-rack ~08:05-08:10, they said minor disruption expected for a minute or two. But kubelet started evicting ~7 minutes later which seems like the probe had a lower tolerance window.

jen: @net-team reported a micro-flap with increased latency/jitter on RDMA-enabled links. Only hosts with Mellanox stacks and jumbo MTU enabled were affected. Non-RDMA nodes mostly fine.

sre-bot: [alert] node-uw2-gpu-12 marked NetworkUnavailable at 1761237420, 2 additional nodes similar — auto-eviction triggered (policy=evict-on-network-fail).

ana: looks like the health probe is too sensitive for RDMA/jumbo setups. We should avoid global evictions for short-lived link flaps. Options: 1) increase failure threshold for the net probe 2) add jitter/debounce to transition to NetworkUnavailable 3) exempt GPU pools from net-probe-driven evictions temporarily.

mike: agreed. I can push a conservative change to kubelet-prober config in the daemonset: failureThreshold 5 -> 10, intervalSeconds 5 -> 10, and add a rolling window median filter. That should avoid 1-2 minute flaps causing NodeCondition flips.

devon: can you draft the exact patch? We need to coordinate with net-team so they know this isn't hiding real incidents. Also we must avoid letting a true prolonged outage persist without evictions.

mike: proposed patch snippet (daemonset config):
```
netProbe:
  enabled: true
  intervalSeconds: 10       # increase probe interval
  failureThreshold: 10      # tolerate short blips
  timeoutSeconds: 3
  jitterWindowMs: 300       # median filter window
```
I'll send as PR to infra-config and tag @net-team for review.

jen: for immediate mitigation we can add a temporary pod disruption exemption annotation to gpu node pools so kube-controller won't evict GPU-backed workloads on NetworkUnavailable alone. But that's a heavy hammer.

ana: let's avoid patchy workarounds. Plan: mike opens PR for prober tuning + add logic to controller to require >5m continuous NetworkUnavailable before eviction for labeled gpu nodes. Then run a small canary in us-west-2 (5 nodes) for a day.

devon: sounds good. Also can we add metric dashboards for net-probe jitter/packet-loss by AZ+node role so we can see correlation before node condition flips? Right now it's buried in node logs.

mike: will add Grafana panels and an alert that fires when net-probe loss >20% for >2m but not immediately evict. Alert will page infra on sustained issues.

jen: FYI, also double-check CNI MTU config across GPU hosts. Some hosts had MTU mismatch after the firmware push which can spike loss for large RDMA packets. If net-team can confirm MTU consistency we'll reduce risk.

devon: net-team confirmed MTU mismatch on one rack and fixed it at 08:18; after that we saw no further evictions. But the damage was done earlier.

ana: timeline + action items then:
- mike: PR to increase prober thresholds + median filter (owner)
- mike: add Grafana panels + alert (owner)
- jen: add controller change to require 5m continuous NetworkUnavailable before eviction for gpu-labeled nodes (owner)
- infra/sre: run a canary rollout (5 nodes) and monitor for 24h
- net-team: confirm MTU and RDMA configs post-firmware (owner)

mike: I'll open the PRs in the next hour and drop links here.

devon: thanks. also logging request: if we ever see net-probe >20% then include the interface counters (RX dropped TX errors) in the auto-debug bundle to speed diagnosis.

jen: good call. I'll add that to the node debug script.

ana: agreed, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene if canary shows any regressions. :thumbsup:
